einzeiler: Why perseverance alone is not enough and how environments shape success.
kurzfassung: Psychologist Angela Duckworth examines why perseverance alone is often insufficient for success. She discusses the significant impact of environments, habits, and peer pressure on human achievement. Additionally, she explores the influence of new technologies on thinking and when changing situations matters more than changing oneself.
stichpunkte: The limitations of perseverance and grit in achieving goals
How environments shape personal development and success
Strategies for making good habits easier to maintain
The role of parents and the types of questions they ask about children
How peer pressure can function as a positive force
The potential impact of AI on human thinking
When changing a situation is more effective than changing oneself
beschreibung:
What if trying harder is sometimes exactly the wrong thing to do?
Angela Duckworth, University of Pennsylvania psychologist, MacArthur Fellow, and author of the #1 New York Times bestseller Grit, has spent years studying achievement. In her new book, Situated, she explores why perseverance alone isn't enough.
She discusses:
How Angela and her husband nearly “gritted” their way out of their marriage
How much your environment shapes who you become
The small change that can make good habits easier
Why parents may be asking the wrong question about their children
How peer pressure can become a force for good
Whether AI could make us worse at thinking
When changing your situation matters more than changing yourself

We spend enormous energy trying to improve ourselves. Angela Duckworth asks a different question: what if the more important thing is to change what’s around us?
